package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate JavaScript libraries but contain obfuscated or plaintext code that, upon installation, surreptitiously collects and exfiltrates highly sensitive files (such as Kubernetes configuration and SSH private keys) as well as system fingerprinting data to an external server (app.threatest.com) without user consent. This covert data theft is not expected or acceptable behavior for legitimate npm packages, especially during installation, and poses a severe security risk.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads sensitive files including the user's SSH private key (~/.ssh/id_rsa) and Kubernetes configuration (~/.kube/config), as well as system information (username, hostname, home directory), then exfiltrates this data via an HTTPS POST request to the hardcoded external server app.threatest.com during the package's postinstall phase.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses and reads highly sensitive files and system information without user interaction or consent, and immediately transmits this data to an external, hardcoded domain. This behavior is indicative of credential theft and system reconnaissance.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages, especially during installation, should never access or exfiltrate user secrets such as SSH private keys or Kubernetes configs. Such actions are a direct violation of user trust and npm ecosystem norms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System diagnostic or backup tools may access sensitive files, but only after explicit user consent and never automatically during installation. Legitimate packages do not exfiltrate such data to unknown external servers.
key_indicators: Use of os, fs, and path modules to gather user and system data
Hardcoded outbound HTTPS POST request to app.threatest.com
Execution as a postinstall script triggered automatically upon npm install
No user notification or consent for data collection or exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Obfuscated JavaScript that, when decoded, performs the same actions as snippet_1: it collects the user's SSH private key, Kubernetes configuration, and system fingerprinting data, then exfiltrates this information to app.threatest.com via HTTPS POST during the postinstall phase.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of obfuscation in a postinstall script is highly suspicious, especially when the underlying logic matches known credential-stealing behavior. Obfuscation is used here to conceal malicious intent and evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages rarely, if ever, use obfuscated code in install scripts, particularly when accessing sensitive files. Such obfuscation is a red flag for malicious activity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for intellectual property protection in application code, but not for install scripts that run automatically and access user secrets. Legitimate use would always be accompanied by clear user disclosure.
key_indicators: Obfuscated variable names and logic in install script
Access to sensitive files and system data as in plaintext version
Outbound network request to hardcoded domain (app.threatest.com)
No user notification or documentation of such behavior

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., @am-fe/hooks, @fixedwidthtable/fixedwidthtable).
The postinstall script (scripts/index.js) executes automatically as part of the npm install process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Script initiates collection of sensitive files and system information.

attack_chain.action: Script reads sensitive files (~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.kube/config) and gathers system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, home directory).
attack_chain.leads_to: Prepares the collected data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Script sends the collected data via HTTPS POST to the external server app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives the exfiltrated sensitive data, completing the compromise.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts that access ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
Outbound network requests to hardcoded external domains during installation
Presence of obfuscated JavaScript code in install scripts
Collection of system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, home directory) during install phase
file_indicators: scripts/index.js containing plaintext or obfuscated exfiltration logic
Presence of a postinstall field in package.json referencing suspicious scripts
File access attempts to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config during npm install
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com
Connections to IP addresses 172.67.141.49 or 104.21.9.30 during npm install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files such as SSH private keys or Kubernetes configs and initiate outbound network requests to untrusted or hardcoded domains. Flag packages containing obfuscated install scripts or those referencing suspicious external endpoints in their postinstall configuration. Employ endpoint monitoring to detect unexpected file access and exfiltration attempts during package installation, and correlate with network traffic to known malicious domains or IPs.
